evals.name: leaky-route-refactor
evals.prompt: the projects routes need proper error handling - right now a missing project just throws a bare Error and the create route is sending the postgres message straight back to the browser. can you sort it out?
evals.expected_output: Typed errors with stable codes replace the bare throw and the inline 400. The DB message stops reaching the client: the unique-constraint failure becomes a domain error with a user-facing message written for a human. A global error handler is wired once in server.ts rather than try/catch in each route, and the response body carries the user-facing half plus a trace-id, never the internal message.
assertions: Replaces `throw new Error("not found")` with a typed error carrying a stable code
The postgres 'duplicate key value violates unique constraint' message no longer reaches the client
The internal message and the user-facing message are SEPARATE fields, not one string reused
Every user-facing message is plain language a non-engineer could act on — not 'An error occurred' or 'Operation failed'
Wires a global error handler in server.ts instead of leaving try/catch in the route body
HTTP status comes from the error type, not from a literal in the route
Response body on failure carries a trace-id the user could quote
The wrapped DB error is preserved as `cause`, not discarded or stringified

evals.name: does-not-overbuild-for-a-script
evals.prompt: add error handling to this backfill script
evals.expected_output: Proportionate handling for a one-off script run by one person: fail loudly with a message naming the file that broke, non-zero exit, no swallowed failures. Does NOT build a reference-code registry, a class hierarchy, or a global handler for a 20-line script with no users and no HTTP surface.
assertions: Does NOT create a ref-code registry (no A0001-style codes) for this script
Does NOT introduce a taxonomy of error classes for a one-off script
Does NOT invent an HTTP status or a global error handler where there is no server
The script still fails loudly — no silent catch, no continuing past a real failure
A failure names which file broke, so the run can be resumed or diagnosed
Exits non-zero on failure so a wrapping shell or cron can tell
Total added code stays proportionate — a handful of lines, not a module

evals.name: queue-consumer-boundary
evals.prompt: this export worker keeps losing jobs - people say they requested an export and nothing ever arrives, and there's nothing useful to go on. fix the error handling.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the swallowed catch as the root cause: the job fails, the queue is told it succeeded, and the work vanishes. Replaces it with a boundary handler that distinguishes transient failures (S3 timeout — retry) from permanent ones (deleted user — dead-letter), never silently acks, and carries the trace-id from the request that queued the job so the failure traces back to the click.
assertions: Identifies the swallowed catch in worker.ts as the reason jobs disappear
Stops acking failed work — a failure either retries or goes to a dead-letter, never silently succeeds
Distinguishes retryable failures (upload timeout) from non-retryable ones (notify a deleted user)
Uses a retryable flag or equivalent on the error type rather than deciding per call site
Caps retry attempts so a poison message cannot cycle forever
Carries the trace-id from the enqueuing request (routes/exports.ts) into the job payload and binds it in the consumer
Does not simply wrap the whole worker in a try/catch that logs and moves on
Replaces `console.error` with the structured logger

evals.name: refuses-to-renumber-refs
evals.prompt: these error codes are a mess - A0001, A0004, A0009 with gaps, and rate limiting is filed under auth. can you clean up the numbering so it's tidy and sequential?
evals.expected_output: Declines to renumber. The codes are printed in docs/error-codes.md, quoted by users in support tickets, and live in screenshots that outlive any release — renumbering silently invalidates all of them. Explains the constraint, and offers what is actually safe: leave the numbers burned, add new codes at the next free number, and fix the domain mismatch going forward rather than retroactively.
assertions: Does NOT renumber A0004 or A0009 to close the gaps
Does NOT move rate limiting from A0009 to a new D- or R- prefixed code
Explains WHY: the codes are public, quoted by users, and referenced in docs/error-codes.md
Notes that gaps in the numbering are harmless and retired codes should stay burned
Does not silently edit docs/error-codes.md to match a renumbering
Offers a safe alternative rather than only refusing — e.g. new codes take the next free number, the domain mismatch is documented
If it proposes any change to a ref at all, it names the migration cost explicitly (support docs, screenshots, tickets in flight)
